title: [VSC-21a] VS Code: remember seat shell pids so a reload or extension restart never deregisters a live seat
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse). Carved out of VSC-21 (task-7e7bd0ec91ca488da2858f70cff32f65) by its architect on 2026-11-02 as a prerequisite. VSC-21 dependsOn this row and wires it into extension.ts. Nothing else depends on it.

Why: VS Code terminals can outlive the extension session that launched their seats.
- A window reload keeps persistent terminal sessions running. terminal.integrated.enablePersistentSessions is on by default, and extension-created terminals persist unless they are created with isTransient.
- "Restart Extensions" after an extension update restarts only the extension host, and every terminal keeps running.
JetBrains tabs die with the IDE. That is why AgentSeatTracker (VSC-20, moe-vscode/src/util/AgentSeatTracker.ts) counts every saved seat as gone at startup and deregisters it at the first connect. Wired in as-is, VSC-21 would therefore deregister live seats after every reload or Moe update, and the daemon would release tasks that their agents are still working on.
The fix: remember each seat's shell pid (vscode Terminal.processId). At activation, before the first connect, mark launched() every saved seat whose shell is still alive.

Deliverable 1: new moe-vscode/src/util/SeatSurvival.ts. It is pure like AgentSeatTracker.ts: no import, no 'vscode' text and no 'require(' text; every dependency is a parameter.
- `isProcessAlive(pid: number, kill = (p, s) => process.kill(p, s)): boolean` probes with signal 0. A positive safe-integer pid is alive when the probe succeeds or throws EPERM, and dead on ESRCH or any other throw. Any other pid is never probed and counts as dead, because process.kill(0 or a negative pid) addresses process groups.
- `class SeatPids(load: () => unknown, save: (pids: Record<string, number>) => void)`, with these methods:
  - `record(workerId, pid: number | undefined)`;
  - `keep(workerIds)`;
  - `seatOf(pid): string | undefined`;
  - `surviving(workerIds, isAlive): string[]`.
  Pids live in a Map, never in an object keyed by worker id. load() is untyped workspace JSON.
VSC-21 consumes it as follows: it persists the map under context.workspaceState key moe.agentSeatPids, calls keep() with every list the tracker saves, calls record() when a launched terminal's processId resolves, calls surviving() at activation, and uses seatOf() to map a surviving or reconnected terminal back to its worker.

Deliverable 2: new moe-vscode/tests/seat-survival.test.cjs. It loads the source under node:vm with a require map that throws on every name, as tests/agent-seat-tracker.test.cjs does.

Not in scope:
- extension.ts, AgentLauncher.ts and MoeDaemonClient.ts (all VSC-21).
- AgentSeatTracker.ts and moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-seat-tracker.json. They stay unchanged: survival is a VS Code adaptation outside the tracker, and the tracker still matches JetBrains on every corpus row.
- Any moe-jetbrains file. JetBrains' analogue, a dynamic plugin reload that keeps tabs alive, is a note for VSC-18, not a fix here.

Verification (GLOBAL rail: never npm in the shared checkout): `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo into a fresh directory outside the checkout and overlay this task's files. Then, in <snapshot>/moe-vscode, run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` under `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl).
definitionOfDone: New moe-vscode/src/util/SeatSurvival.ts exports isProcessAlive(pid, kill?) and class SeatPids(load, save) with record(workerId, pid), keep(workerIds), seatOf(pid) and surviving(workerIds, isAlive). The file has no import and no 'require(' or 'vscode' text, and it loads under a require map that throws on every module name.

isProcessAlive probes a positive safe-integer pid with signal 0. It returns true when the probe succeeds or throws EPERM, and false on ESRCH or any other throw. For 0, negative, fractional, NaN, non-number or undefined pids it returns false without probing. This is proven with a recording kill stub, plus one real probe of process.pid that returns true.

SeatPids loads only positive safe-integer pids under non-blank worker ids from a plain object; an array, string, number, null or undefined loads nothing. record keeps one worker per pid, so a reused pid moves to the new worker, and an invalid pid records nothing. keep drops every worker not in the list, and a non-array list keeps none. save runs only when the map changed and receives a fresh object each time.

surviving returns exactly the given worker ids whose recorded pid isAlive confirms, in the order given and once each. It never calls isAlive for an id without a recorded pid, and it returns [] for a non-array.
New moe-vscode/tests/seat-survival.test.cjs proves items 1-4 with exact-value assertions. A scratch-copy mutant in which surviving ignores isAlive makes it fail; the mutant is discarded afterwards.
In a git-archive snapshot of HEAD plus this diff, `cd moe-vscode && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` exits 0 with 0 failures.

implementationPlan.note: Wrote tests/seat-survival.test.cjs (S1, S2a-c, S3a-e, S4a-d, S5a-c, S6a-e) with the Write tool. RED confirmed in place with plain node --test: ENOENT on src/util/SeatSurvival.ts. Beyond the plan rows I pinned: isAlive receives exactly one argument (so a function passed straight in never gets a second one), a dead duplicate id is probed once, and a real exited-process pid is dead under the default kill. No npm run in the shared checkout. Dirty paths from other sessions untouched.

Wrote src/util/SeatSurvival.ts with the Write tool: private isPid, isProcessAlive(pid: unknown, kill = process.kill probe) and class SeatPids over a private Map (assign/persist helpers; record, keep, seatOf, surviving). No import, no require text, no editor-name text (grep count 0). In-place `node --test tests/seat-survival.test.cjs`: 21 pass, 0 fail. Note for VSC-21 recorded in the module JSDoc: a recycled pid only delays deregistration.

implementationPlan.description:
Gate and mutation proof, run once (DoD 5 and 6; mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl).

1. Run exactly executionContract.checkRefs[0]. It builds the snapshot /tmp/vsc21a-gate from `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo plus this task's two files, then runs npm ci, lint, compile and the full npm test under env -i with nvm Node 24. Expect exit 0 and 0 failures. The baseline at 9ea87aa6 was 416 tests, 412 pass, 4 skip, before later landings and the new rows.
2. Then, in that snapshot only: make surviving ignore isAlive in the SNAPSHOT copy of src/util/SeatSurvival.ts with one exact replacement (assert the count is 1). Run `node --test tests/seat-survival.test.cjs` there and confirm that S6 fails by assertion. Then delete the snapshot.

Submit the gate command, its exit code and the output tail as the complete_task verification.

Error handling for a red gate: read the first failing assertion. A failure in another suite is a real regression. A MODULE_NOT_FOUND before any assertion is a snapshot mistake (wrong cwd or missing overlay).
implementationPlan.note: Ran executionContract.checkRefs[0] verbatim: git-archive snapshot /tmp/vsc21a-gate + the two new files, then npm ci, lint (eslint src), compile (tsc -p ./), npm test under env -i with nvm Node 24: exit 0, 472 tests, 468 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail (baseline 416 before later landings plus 21 new rows). Mutant in the SNAPSHOT copy only (exactly 1 replacement: surviving ignores isAlive): S6a, S6b, S6c, S6d, S6e fail by assertion (e.g. actual ['w2','w1'] vs expected ['w1']); other 16 rows pass. Snapshot and log deleted; the shared checkout was never mutated and no npm ran in it.

Self-review of the two-new-file diff.
(1) Purity: grep for the editor name, require( and ^import in SeatSurvival.ts = 0/0/0; no forbidden pattern in either file.
(2) Throws: isProcessAlive wraps the probe in try/catch and reads err.code through (err as {code?: unknown} | null)?.code. Only the injected load/save/isAlive can throw, and their errors propagate unchanged (S3e).
(3) Invariants: all writes go through assign(), which deletes any other holder of the pid before setting, so one worker per pid and one pid per worker hold after every record and after load. Deleting from a Map during its iteration is safe in JS.
(4) save fires only when the map changed (record compares prev pid; keep flags a drop) and receives Object.fromEntries(map), a fresh object (S4d proves a mutation does not reach the map).
(5) Prototype-named ids ('constructor', 'hasOwnProperty', 'toString') stay plain data because of the Map (S3d).
(6) Every DoD item has exact-value assertions; every stub (killStub, aliveTable, the save recorder) records before acting.
(7) Scope: only moe-vscode/src/util/SeatSurvival.ts (124 lines) and tests/seat-survival.test.cjs (300 lines, trimmed from 318 by merging rows, no assertion dropped) are new. AgentSeatTracker.ts, client-seat-tracker.json, extension.ts and AgentLauncher.ts show an empty git diff.
Theoretical only, left as is: a re-entrant record() from inside save would just mutate the map again (single-threaded, no corruption); a recycled pid can keep a dead seat looking alive, which only delays its deregistration (noted in the module JSDoc for VSC-21); S2c/S6 spawn one short-lived node child to get a dead pid, and a pid reuse within milliseconds is practically impossible on sequential pid allocation.
Final gate re-run on the trimmed bytes: exit 0, 470 tests, 466 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail. Mutant (surviving ignores isAlive, snapshot copy, 1 replacement) fails S2c, S6a-S6d by assertion; snapshot deleted. Shared-checkout dirty paths from other sessions untouched.

comments.content:
@architect-0fcb7226 I created this row while planning VSC-21 (task-7e7bd0ec, now WORKING and gated on this row). VSC-21's plan already codes against this API, so please keep these exact shapes:
- `export function isProcessAlive(pid: number, kill?: ...): boolean`. The second parameter must be optional, because extension.ts passes isProcessAlive directly where `(pid: number) => boolean` is expected.
- `export class SeatPids`, constructed as `new SeatPids(() => context.workspaceState.get('moe.agentSeatPids'), pids => persist(...))`, so load returns unknown.
- `record(workerId: string, pid: number | undefined)`. VSC-21 passes Terminal.processId's result, which can be undefined.
- `keep(workerIds)`, called with every list AgentSeatTracker saves.
- `seatOf(pid: number | undefined): string | undefined`, called with processId results.
- `surviving(workerIds, isAlive): string[]`, called with `context.workspaceState.get<string[]>('moe.agentSeats', [])`, which may be any JSON at runtime.
Purity: same as AgentSeatTracker.ts (no import, no 'require(' or 'vscode' text). Copy the tests/agent-seat-tracker.test.cjs harness. Background is in mem:gotcha-vscode-terminals-outlive-extension-host and mem:task-task-7e7bd0ec91ca488da2858f70cff32f65-handoff. For the DoD-5 mutant, the recipe in mem:convention-vscode-port-mutant-checkref works: append an override such as `SeatPids.prototype.surviving = function (ids) { ... }` to a scratch copy, which is deterministic whatever the formatting.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A pure module remembers each launched seat's shell pid and answers which saved seats still have a live shell. VSC-21 can then keep those seats instead of deregistering them after a window reload or an extension-host restart.
acceptanceCriteria: isProcessAlive probes only positive safe-integer pids with signal 0: alive on success or EPERM, dead on ESRCH or any other throw.
SeatPids keeps one worker per pid in a Map, loads only valid entries from a plain object, saves a fresh object only on change, and keep with a non-array keeps none.
surviving returns, in input order and once each, the ids whose recorded pid isAlive confirms with true, and never calls isAlive for an unrecorded id.
invariants: SeatSurvival.ts has no import, no 'require(' text and no 'vscode' text.
AgentSeatTracker.ts, moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-seat-tracker.json, extension.ts, AgentLauncher.ts and MoeDaemonClient.ts are unchanged.
No method throws except by propagating an injected load or save error.
sourceAssumptions: moe-vscode/src/util/AgentSeatTracker.ts is pure and lets injected callbacks own their errors; tests/agent-seat-tracker.test.cjs loads it through vm.runInThisContext with a throwing require.
process.kill(pid, 0) throws ESRCH for a missing process and EPERM for one owned by another user, and returns true otherwise.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
The module goes straight to the description's API; no alternatives are needed, since the row was carved out with a fixed interface for VSC-21. Decisions made explicit:
- surviving treats only a strict `true` as confirmation.
- load applies record's one-worker-per-pid rule, so the invariant holds from construction.
- keep with a non-array clears the map.
- Construction never saves, even when load filtered entries out.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- AgentSeatTracker.ts (VSC-20, 161c058c) is the template: pure, no imports, and the callbacks own their errors.
- tests/agent-seat-tracker.test.cjs loads its module with vm.runInThisContext and a throwing require, and its purity row uses /vscode/i (case-insensitive), so comments must avoid the word too.
- moe-vscode tsconfig is lib ES2020 and strict with no types restriction, so Object.fromEntries and the process global compile; eslint flat/recommended applies.
- Gate baseline at 9ea87aa6: 416 tests / 412 pass / 4 skip.
planningNotes.risks:
- Pid reuse can make a dead seat look alive. That direction is safe (deregistration is only delayed), and VSC-21 may add a launch-time check.
- A test that uses a kill stub throwing a plain object instead of an Error must still read .code.
- Never spell the prototype-pollution key in the source or the test (project forbiddenPatterns); 'constructor' and 'hasOwnProperty' cover the Map choice.
- Do not touch AgentSeatTracker.ts or the shared corpus.
